record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: Can compressed-communication and sparse-update methods developed for centrally orchestrated federated learning be translated to fully decentralized learning without harming convergence, while also enabling better privacy-utility trade-offs than local differential privacy alone?

evidence.quote: without negatively impacting the convergence is an active research direction

artifact.category_tag: decentralized federated learning with compression and differential privacy
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a fully decentralized learning setting in which $n$ agents (nodes) are arranged on a connected undirected communication graph $G=(V,E)$, with $|V|=n$. Each agent $i\in V$ holds a local data distribution $\mathcal{D}_i$ and a local loss $F_i(	heta)=\mathbb{E}_{z\sim \mathcal{D}_i}[\ell(	heta;z)]$ for parameter $	heta\in\mathbb{R}^d$, and the agents collectively wish to minimize $F(	heta)= rac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n F_i(	heta)$. Communication is restricted to neighbors in $G$; there is no central server.

In each round $t$, every agent $i$ performs (possibly stochastic) local updates and then communicates with neighbors a message $m_{i	o j}^{(t)} = \mathcal{C}(g_i^{(t)})$, where $g_i^{(t)}\in\mathbb{R}^d$ is an update vector (e.g., a stochastic gradient or model delta) and $\mathcal{C}:\mathbb{R}^d	o\mathcal{M}$ is a (possibly randomized) compression operator (such as quantization, top-$k$ sparsification, or sketching) with bounded message size $b(\mathcal{C})\ll d$ bits. Sparse-update methods further restrict $g_i^{(t)}$ to lie in a low-dimensional subset (a coordinate mask) chosen by each agent.

For privacy, an algorithm is said to satisfy local differential privacy with parameter $\varepsilon>0$ if, for every agent $i$, the entire transcript of messages $i$ sends to its neighbors is $\varepsilon$-DP with respect to $i$'s local dataset. More generally, one may consider distributed/network differential privacy, where the privacy guarantee is taken with respect to the view of any colluding subset of agents.

The problem has two parts.

(a) Construct a decentralized optimization algorithm using a compression operator $\mathcal{C}$ and/or sparse-update masks that, under standard assumptions (e.g., $L$-smoothness of each $F_i$, bounded gradient variance, mixing properties of the gossip matrix associated with $G$), achieves the same asymptotic convergence rate (in expectation, to a stationary point for nonconvex $F$, or to the optimum for convex $F$) as the corresponding uncompressed centrally orchestrated federated algorithm, while using only $O(b(\mathcal{C}))$ bits per agent per round.

(b) Show that such a decentralized compressed algorithm can be combined with a privacy mechanism so that, for a fixed end-to-end privacy budget $\varepsilon$ against an adversary controlling a strict subset of agents, the resulting privacy-utility trade-off (excess loss as a function of $\varepsilon$ and $n$) is strictly better than what is achievable by any algorithm satisfying $\varepsilon$-local differential privacy at each agent.

Provide such an algorithm together with matching upper and lower bounds, or prove that no such algorithm exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a stated open research direction in the federated learning literature. There has been substantial progress on compressed decentralized SGD (e.g., CHOCO-SGD, DeepSqueeze, Quantized Gossip), and on network/secure-aggregation differential privacy that outperforms local DP, but a fully unified solution matching centralized-FL convergence rates with provably better privacy-utility trade-offs in arbitrary decentralized topologies remains an active open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Lists compressed communication, sparse updates, and decentralized privacy as active open research directions.
status_evidence.claim: The translation of compression/sparsification techniques to fully decentralized settings with improved privacy-utility trade-offs is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Decentralized Stochastic Optimization and Gossip Algorithms with Compressed Communication (Koloskova et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: CHOCO-SGD achieves convergence for decentralized SGD with arbitrary compression operators.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists on compressed decentralized optimization with convergence guarantees, but combined privacy-utility optimality is unresolved.
